diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal G=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ c^2(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}

issues.failure_explanation: The appendix counterexample uses endpoint states whose second or first partial density is zero. The admissible set G is defined with the strict inequalities z1ρ1>0 and z2ρ2>0, so neither displayed endpoint state belongs to G. Therefore the constructed midpoint does not demonstrate non-convexity of G as defined.

failure_location.quote: that the admissible set $\mathcal{G}$ is non-convex.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pure-phase endpoint states by states with small positive partial densities satisfying G, or otherwise construct valid endpoints, and re-verify that the midpoint has c^2<0; if no such perturbation is available, withdraw the non-convexity claim.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that Appendix A supplies a concrete counterexample proving G is non-convex is unsupported. This weakens the stated motivation for the stricter admissible set G^p, although it does not by itself invalidate the convexity theorem for G^p.
issues.title: Invalid non-convexity counterexample for G
issues.why_classification: The defect is local to the counterexample. A standard perturbation or withdrawal of the side claim can repair the issue without affecting the main BP, Abgrall, or convergence results.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof applies the intermediate value theorem, which requires F to be continuous on [0,1]. The source term f contains κ and ν_k, while ν_k is defined as 1/(γ_k(p^{n+1}+p_{w,k})) and can be undefined or discontinuous if p(z)+p_{w,k}=0 for some z in [0,1]. The theorem only assumes z1^n∈[0,1], so the needed continuity/regularity of f is neither assumed nor proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a local regularity/admissibility hypothesis, for example p(z)+p_{w,k}>0 for k=1,2 and all z∈[0,1], or prove continuity of f under the paper's admissible-state assumptions before invoking the intermediate value theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The stated existence of a bounded updated volume fraction for the implicit κ-step is unsupported for non-admissible pressure states. The omitted BP proof for the adaptive solver inherits the same gap because it relies on the same implicit root-finding argument.
issues.title: Implicit BP proof assumes unestablished continuity
issues.why_classification: This is a missing standard local condition in the proof. Adding the condition preserves the volume-fraction BP conclusion for physically admissible states and does not change the method's advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed θ_p formula is valid only if pressure is affine along the segment U_avg+θ(U_tilde-U_avg). For the Tammann EOS, p(U) is a ratio of affine functions and is not affine. Concrete counterexample: in 1D with u=0, fixed positive partial densities, γ1=1.5, γ2=2, p_w1=4.5, p_w2=5, E=11.9, one obtains p(z)=(1.9-3.5z)/(1+z). Take the average state with z=0.2, p=1, and the tilted state with z=0.8, p=-0.5. Then ε_p=10^{-13} and θ_p≈2/3. The limited state has z≈0.6 and p≈-0.125<ε_p. Thus the algorithm can output a state outside G^p, contradicting the stated post-limiter bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the linear θ_p formula by a pressure-specific BP construction that enforces p≥ε_p at all quadrature points (or otherwise guarantees p>0), and must also handle non-admissible cell averages; otherwise the pressure BP claim must be withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised bound-preserving property for pressure is false as written, and the claim that the BP limiter output satisfies U_ingp is unsupported. This undermines the central BP guarantee for pressure in the abstract and introduction.
issues.title: Pressure BP limiter formula does not enforce pressure positivity
issues.why_classification: The displayed pressure limiter is mathematically insufficient for the nonlinear Tammann pressure. Preserving the central pressure BP guarantee requires a new nontrivial construction not supplied by the source, while the source-supported alternative is to abandon a central advertised guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For all cases, we simply employ $\Delta t \propto \Delta x$ and $CFL=0.1$.
While formally restricted to second-order temporal accuracy
the resulting temporal error remains subdominant to the overall error.

issues.failure_explanation: The text states that the operator splitting restricts temporal accuracy to second order and that Δt is proportional to Δx. With Δt=O(Δx), a second-order temporal error is O(Δx^2). For DG(P^2), the spatial error is O(Δx^3), so the temporal error cannot be subdominant asymptotically. The source therefore does not support the claim that the P^2 method with Δt∝Δx exhibits third-order convergence.

failure_location.quote: still exhibits the expected third-order convergence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to second-order convergence for Δt∝Δx, consistent with the acknowledged temporal restriction, or provide new experiments/analysis with Δt=O(Δx^3) or a proof that the temporal error is subdominant.
issues.overall_effect: The stated optimal convergence rate for the P^2 smooth gas-gas test is unreliable. The numerical accuracy verification overclaims the order achieved under the used time-step scaling.
issues.title: Third-order convergence claim inconsistent with second-order time-step scaling
issues.why_classification: The source supports a limited weakening to the explicitly acknowledged second-order temporal behavior. The main spatial discretization and BP guarantees remain, but the advertised third-order rate under the stated scaling is lost.
